title: Plunge into a stellar ocean
caption: The IC4701 nebula, imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope
credit: ESO/VPHAS+ team. Acknowledgement: Cambridge Astronomical Survey Unit

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Intense reddish gas and dark clouds of dust mingle with a crowd of stars in this view of the IC4701 nebula in the constellation Sagittarius. On the sky, the nebula spans twice the width of the full Moon.

The red color comes from hydrogen. Energetic light from newborn stars ionizes the gas, and it responds by shining in that particular reddish hue. The dark clouds are rich in interstellar dust, so thick that light from the stars behind them cannot get through.

IC4701 is part of a vast complex of dust and gas where new stars are springing to life. Most stars are born cooler, redder and less massive than the Sun. Hot, massive stars are much rarer and burn through their fuel quickly before dying. That short life makes brilliant blue massive stars, and the glowing gas around them, signposts of recent star formation.

understand.summary: The VLT Survey Telescope's OmegaCAM camera recorded this visible-light image through u, g, r and i filters plus a hydrogen-alpha filter. The color mapping isn't published.
